title: Letters change shape: initial / medial / final / isolated forms
objectives: Student can explain that most Arabic letters take up to 4 different shapes depending on position in a word (isolated / initial / medial / final), while the sound stays the same.
Student can recognize a letter's initial, medial, and final forms on sight for at least 6 high-frequency letters.
Student can read a short 2–3 letter connected (unvoweled) cluster by recognizing each component letter regardless of its shape-shifted form.

slides.heading: Lesson 1.7 — Letters change shape: initial / medial / final / isolated forms

audio.cue: ا: an open, unobstructed sound from deep in the chest cavity — no closure anywhere, just a clear open vowel
lips fully together
tongue-tip on gum ridge
tongue between teeth
ح: a strong, breathy, unvoiced friction from the middle of the throat — like fogging a mirror from deep in the throat, no English equivalent
خ: a rasping fricative from the upper throat/back of the tongue against the soft palate — a genuine back-of-throat 'kh', not softened
د: tongue-tip taps the upper gum ridge firmly — a plain, crisp 'd'
ذ: tongue-tip between the teeth, same point as ث but VOICED — 'th' as in 'this', never a 'z'

audio.title: Arabic101 Makharij Lesson 10 — ر (ra), the ULTIMATE guide

audio.cue: ز: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a plain buzzing 'z' — voiced twin of س
س: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a thin hiss — a plain 's'
ش: middle of tongue against the roof of the mouth, a soft 'sh'
ع: a mid-throat muscular squeeze, voiced — no equivalent sound in English or Turkic languages
غ: upper throat, same zone as خ but voiced — a uvular fricative, like a French uvular 'r'
ف: inner lower lip against the edge of the upper front teeth — a plain 'f'
ك: back of tongue against the soft palate, shallower in the mouth than ق — a plain 'k'
م: the two lips, with nasal resonance — 'm'
ه: a light, breathy throat release — a soft 'h', much gentler than ح
و: rounded lips — a consonant 'w'
ي: middle of tongue toward the roof of the mouth — a consonant 'y'

slides.heading: Letters change shape — but never their sound
body: A letter's sound never changes, no matter where it sits in a word.
But many letters' SHAPE changes depending on position: isolated, word-initial, word-medial, or word-final.
Today's focus letters: the dotted-body group ب ت ث ن ي (near-identical connecting body, differ mainly by dot count/position) plus ك ل م for contrast (more visually distinct positional forms).

slides.heading: Worked example: ب in all 4 positions
body: Same dot, different body shape depending on position.
Isolated: ب — no connections on either side.
Initial (starts a word, connects forward only): بـ

dailyChecklist: Write today's 8 letters (ب ت ث ن ي ك ل م) in all forms (isolated/initial/medial/final) 4 rows each in your notebook, saying the name and sound aloud as you write

script: Open with a full 28-letter cumulative shuffle before introducing positional shape-shifting.
Model ب's four position forms side by side first — same dot, different body — before the ت/ث/ن/ي and ك/ل/م groups.
Run the guided recognition drill on all 8 focus letters before moving to 2-letter cluster reading.
Confirm the concept generalizes with a few non-focus Unit 1.1 letters (ح ص ق) in position-form, not just today's 8.
Watch for left-to-right reading habit carrying over from the student's other literacy — correct direction slips immediately, especially on the very first cluster.
Treat isolated-shape reversion in medial position as an expected early confusion to coach through, not a graded mistake.
listenFor: Student mentally reverting to isolated-letter shapes and stalling/mis-reading when a letter appears in medial form — common early confusion, expect and coach through it rather than treating it as a "mistake" per se.
Student reading left-to-right out of habit (if their other literacy, Cyrillic/Latin Uzbek, is LTR) — watch for direction slips, especially on the very first cluster of the lesson.

Sounds regressing on letters that were solid in isolation (e.g., ث or ح appearing in a cluster) — confirms whether errors from Unit 1.1 were truly fixed or were "isolation-only" fixes that don't yet transfer to reading context.
teacherNotes.homework: In the student's notebook: today's 8 letters (ب ت ث ن ي ك ل م) written in all forms — isolated, initial, medial, final — 4 full rows per letter, saying name and sound aloud while writing, then memorized; daily re-reading of the 8 two-letter and 4 three-letter clusters from the lesson aloud, 3× through; a review row of 5 previously learned letters written in their forms, name and sound said aloud while writing. No printed sheets.
